questions.problem:
Differentiate $f(t)+g(t)+h(t)$ with respect to $t$, where

$$
\begin{aligned}f(t) & =⟨-1,\,0,\,1⟩ \\ g(t) & =⟨-t,\,0,t⟩ \\ h(t) & =⟨-{t}^{2},0,{t}^{2}⟩\end{aligned}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
Using the sum rule, we can write

$$
(f(t)+g(t)+h(t))^{′}={f}^{′}(t)+{g}^{′}(t)+{h}^{′}(t)
$$

Let's now find the derivatives of each function.

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-1),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(0),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(1)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,0,0⟩ \\ {g}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(0),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t)⟩ \\  & =⟨-1,0,1⟩ \\ {h}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-{t}^{2}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(0),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2})⟩ \\  & =⟨-2t,\,0,\,2t⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}(f(t)+g(t)+h(t))^{′} & ={f}^{′}(t)+{g}^{′}(t)+{h}^{′}(t) \\  & =⟨0,0,0⟩+⟨-1,0,1⟩+⟨-2t,\,0,\,2t⟩ \\  & =⟨-2t-1,\,0,\,2t+1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Differentiate $f(t)+g(t)$ with respect to $t$, given that 

$$
\begin{aligned}f(t) & =⟨3t-1,\,6-t,\,7t⟩ \\ g(t) & =⟨{t}^{2},\,1-{t}^{2},\,t⟩\end{aligned}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
By the sum rule, we have

$$
(f(t)+g(t))^{′}={f}^{′}(t)+{g}^{′}(t)
$$

Let's find the derivatives of each function:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3t-1),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(6-t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(7t)⟩ \\  & =⟨3,\,-1,\,7⟩ \\ {g}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(1-{t}^{2}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t)⟩ \\  & =⟨2t,\,-2t,\,1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}(f(t)+g(t))^{′} & ={f}^{′}(t)+{g}^{′}(t) \\  & =⟨3,\,-1,\,7⟩+⟨2t,\,-2t,\,1⟩ \\  & =⟨2t+3,\,-2t-1,\,8⟩\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Differentiate $2f(t)+3g(t)$ with respect to $t$, where

 

$$
\begin{aligned}f(t) & =2\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,i+3\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,(j-\,k) \\ g(t) & =(5-\operatorname{sin}⁡t)\,i-\,j+2\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,k\end{aligned}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
Using the constant multiple and the sum rules, we have 

$$
(2f(t)+3g(t))^{′}=2{f}^{′}(t)+3{g}^{′}(t)
$$

Let's find the derivatives of each function:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2\operatorname{sin}⁡t)\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3\operatorname{cos}⁡t)\,j-\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3\operatorname{cos}⁡t)\,k \\  & =2\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,i-3\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,j+3\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,k \\ {g}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(5-\operatorname{sin}⁡t)\,i-\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}1\,j+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2\operatorname{cos}⁡t)\,k \\  & =-\operatorname{cos}⁡ti-2\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,k\end{aligned}
$$

Hence 

$$
\begin{aligned}(2f(t)+3g(t))^{′} & =2{f}^{′}(t)+3{g}^{′}(t) \\  & =2(2\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,i-3\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,j+3\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,k)+3(-\operatorname{cos}⁡ti-2\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,k) \\  & =4\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,i-6\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,j+6\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,k-3\operatorname{cos}⁡ti-6\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,k \\  & =\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,i-6\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,j\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Differentiate $f(t)+g(t)$ with respect to $t$, given that 

$$
\begin{aligned}f(t) & =⟨1-2t,\,{t}^{2},\,(t-1)^{2}⟩, \\ g(t) & =⟨t+1,\,1-2t,\,{t}^{3}⟩\end{aligned}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
By the sum rule, we have

$$
(f(t)+g(t))^{′}={f}^{′}(t)+{g}^{′}(t).
$$

Let's find the derivatives of each function:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(1-2t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}((t-1)^{2})⟩ \\  & =⟨-2,\,2t,\,2(t-1)⟩ \\ {g}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t+1),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(1-2t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{3})⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,-2,\,3{t}^{2}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}(f(t)+g(t))^{′} & ={f}^{′}(t)+{g}^{′}(t) \\  & =⟨-2,\,2t,\,2t-2⟩+⟨1,\,-2,\,3{t}^{2}⟩ \\  & =⟨-1,\,2t-2,\,3{t}^{2}+2t-2⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Differentiate $2g(t)-h(t)$ with respect to $t$, where

$$
\begin{aligned}g(t) & =⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,3t-3,\,-{t}^{2}⟩ \\ h(t) & =⟨\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,-t,\,4⟩\end{aligned}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
Using the constant multiple and the sum rules, we have

$$
(2g(t)-h(t))^{′}=2{g}^{′}(t)-{h}^{′}(t)
$$

Let's now find the derivatives of each function.

$$
\begin{aligned}{g}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3t-3),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-{t}^{2})⟩ \\  & =⟨-\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,3,\,-2t⟩ \\ {h}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}4⟩ \\  & =⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,-1,\,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}(2g(t)-h(t))^{′} & =2{g}^{′}(t)-{h}^{′}(t) \\  & =2⟨-\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,3,\,-2t⟩-⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,-1,\,0⟩ \\  & =⟨-2\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,6,\,-4t⟩-⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,-1,\,0⟩ \\  & =⟨-2\operatorname{sin}⁡t-\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,6-(-1),\,-4t-0⟩ \\  & =⟨-2\operatorname{sin}⁡t-\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,7,\,-4t⟩\end{aligned}
$$

questions.worked_solution:
Using the scalar function multiple rule, we can write

$$
(u(t)f(t))^{′}={u}^{′}(t)f(t)+u(t){f}^{′}(t)
$$

Let's find ${u}^{′}(t)$ and ${f}^{′}(t).$

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(t) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡t) \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2t-8) \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({5}^{t})\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡t \\ 2 \\ {5}^{t}\operatorname{ln}⁡5\end{aligned}] \\ {u}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2})=2t\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}(u(t)f(t))^{′} & ={u}^{′}(t)f(t)+u(t){f}^{′}(t) \\  & ={t}^{2}[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡t \\ 2 \\ {5}^{t}\operatorname{ln}⁡5\end{aligned}]+2t[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡t \\ 2t-8 \\ {5}^{t}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}{t}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡t \\ 2{t}^{2} \\ {5}^{t}{t}^{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡5\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}2t\operatorname{sin}⁡t \\ 4{t}^{2}-16t \\ {5}^{t}\cdot 2t\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}{t}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡t+2t\operatorname{sin}⁡t \\ 6{t}^{2}-16t \\ {5}^{t}{t}^{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡5+{5}^{t}\cdot 2t\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Using the chain rule, we can write 

$$
(f∘u)^{′}(t)={f}^{′}(u(t)){u}^{′}(t)
$$

Now, let's find the derivatives of each function.

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(u) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}u}u\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}u}2u\,j+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}3u\,k \\  & =i+2\,j+3\,k \\ {u}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2}) \\  & =2t\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}(f∘u)^{′}(t) & =f′(u(t))u′(t) \\  & =(i+2\,j+3\,k)2t \\  & =2t\,i+4t\,j+6t\,k\end{aligned}
$$

questions.worked_solution:
Using the cross product rule, we can write:

$$
({f}^{′}\times f)^{′}(t)={f}^{″}(t)\times f(t)+{f}^{′}(t)\times {f}^{′}(t)
$$

Let's now find the first and second derivative of the function.

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(1-{t}^{2})\,,\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(1-{t}^{3})\,,\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(1-t)⟩ \\  & =⟨-2t\,,\,-3{t}^{2}\,,\,-1⟩ \\ {f}^{″}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-2t)\,,\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-3{t}^{2})\,,\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-1)⟩ \\  & =⟨-2\,,\,-6t\,,\,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{″}(t)\times f(t) & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ -2 & -6t & 0 \\ 1-{t}^{2} & 1-{t}^{3} & 1-t\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}-6t & 0 \\ 1-{t}^{3} & 1-t\end{aligned}|i-|\begin{aligned}-2 & 0 \\ 1-{t}^{2} & 1-t\end{aligned}|j+|\begin{aligned}-2 & -6t \\ 1-{t}^{2} & 1-{t}^{3}\end{aligned}|k \\  & =⟨-6t+6{t}^{2}\,,\,2-2t\,,\,-2+6t-4{t}^{3}⟩ \\ {f}^{′}(t)\times {f}^{′}(t) & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ -2t & -3{t}^{2} & -1 \\ -2t & -3{t}^{2} & -1\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}-3{t}^{2} & -1 \\ -3{t}^{2} & -1\end{aligned}|i-|\begin{aligned}-2t & -1 \\ -2t & -1\end{aligned}|j+|\begin{aligned}-2t & -3{t}^{2} \\ -2t & -3{t}^{2}\end{aligned}|k \\  & =⟨0\,,\,0\,,\,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally,

$$
\begin{aligned}({f}^{′}\times f)^{′}(t) & =⟨-6t+6{t}^{2}\,,\,2-2t\,,\,-2+6t-4{t}^{3}⟩+⟨0\,,\,0\,,\,0⟩ \\  & =⟨-6t+6{t}^{2}\,,\,2-2t\,,\,-2+6t-4{t}^{3}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Let's find ${v}^{′}(t)$ and ${f}^{′}(t).$

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({2}^{t}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({2}^{t+1}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({2}^{2t}+1)⟩ \\  & =⟨{2}^{t}\operatorname{ln}⁡2,\,{2}^{t+1}\operatorname{ln}⁡2,\,2\cdot {2}^{2t}\operatorname{ln}⁡2⟩ \\ {v}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{1}{{2}^{t}})=-\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}{{2}^{t}}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}(v(t)f(t))^{′} & =v(t){f}^{′}(t)+{v}^{′}(t)f(t) \\  & =\frac{1}{{2}^{t}}⟨{2}^{t}\operatorname{ln}⁡2,\,{2}^{t+1}\operatorname{ln}⁡2,\,2\cdot {2}^{2t}\operatorname{ln}⁡2⟩-\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}{{2}^{t}}⟨{2}^{t},\,{2}^{t+1},\,{2}^{2t}+1⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{{2}^{t}\operatorname{ln}⁡2}{{2}^{t}},\,\frac{{2}^{t+1}\operatorname{ln}⁡2}{{2}^{t}},\,\frac{2\cdot {2}^{2t}\operatorname{ln}⁡2}{{2}^{t}}⟩-⟨\frac{{2}^{t}\operatorname{ln}⁡2}{{2}^{t}},\,\frac{{2}^{t+1}2\operatorname{ln}⁡2}{{2}^{t}},\,\frac{({2}^{2t}+1)\operatorname{ln}⁡2}{{2}^{t}}⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,0,\,\frac{({2}^{2t}-1)\operatorname{ln}⁡2}{{2}^{t}}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

canonical_examples.knowledge_point: Using the Sum and Constant Multiple Rules for Differentiation
canonical_examples.problem:
Find the derivative of $\mathbf f(t) + 2\mathbf g(t)$ with respect to $t,$ where $\mathbf f(t)$ and $\mathbf g(t)$ are defined as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(t) & =(4{t}^{2}+9)\,i-(\frac{1}{t-2})\,j+\operatorname{cos}⁡2t\,k \\ g(t) & =(4t-1)\,i+{e}^{3t}\,j+\operatorname{cos}⁡2t\,k\end{aligned}
$$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
Using the constant multiple rule and the sum rule, we have

$$
(\mathbf f(t) + 2\mathbf g(t))' = \mathbf f'(t) + 2\mathbf g'(t).
$$

Now, let's find the derivative of each function:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(4{t}^{2}+9)\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-\frac{1}{t-2})\,j+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡2t)\,k \\  & =8t\,i+\frac{1}{(t-2)^{2}}\,j-2\operatorname{sin}⁡2t\,k, \\ {g}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(4t-1)\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{3t})j+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡2t)k \\  & =4\,i+3{e}^{3t}\,j-2\operatorname{sin}⁡2t\,k.\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}(f(t)+2g(t))^{′} & ={f}^{′}(t)+2{g}^{′}(t) \\  & =(8t\,i+\frac{1}{(t-2)^{2}}\,j-2\operatorname{sin}⁡2t\,k)+2(4\,i+3{e}^{3t}\,j-2\operatorname{sin}⁡2t\,k) \\  & =8(t+1)\,i+(\frac{1}{(t-2)^{2}}+6{e}^{3t})\,j-6\operatorname{sin}⁡2t\,k.\end{aligned}
$$

canonical_examples.knowledge_point: Using the Scalar Function Multiple Rule for Differentiation
canonical_examples.problem: Find $\big( u(t) \mathbf g(t) \big)'$ where ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14048749/assets/9e23d542bfc56d506f5437a35a92c304d618109ef60086e1f5a7a4fee57d8a80.png) and $u(t) = t.$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
Using the scalar function multiple rule, we have

$$
\big( u(t) \mathbf g(t) \big)' = u'(t) \mathbf{g}(t) + u(t) \mathbf{g}'(t).
$$

Let's find $\mathbf g'(t)$ and $u'(t),$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{g}^{′}(t) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{ln}⁡t) \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-t) \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}{e}^{2t}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{t} \\ -1 \\ 2{e}^{2t}\end{aligned}] \\ {u}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t)=1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}(u(t)g(t))^{′} & ={u}^{′}(t)g(t)+u(t){g}^{′}(t) \\  & =1\cdot [\begin{aligned}\operatorname{ln}⁡t \\ -t \\ {e}^{2t}\end{aligned}]+t\cdot [\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{t} \\ -1 \\ 2{e}^{2t}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{ln}⁡t \\ -t \\ {e}^{2t}\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -t \\ 2t{e}^{2t}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1+\operatorname{ln}⁡t \\ -2t \\ (2t+1){e}^{2t}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

canonical_examples.knowledge_point: Using the Chain Rule for Differentiation
canonical_examples.problem: Find $(\mathbf f \circ u)'(t),$ if $\mathbf f(u) = \ln u \, \mathbf i + (u^2+5) \, \mathbf j + 4u \, \mathbf k$ and $u(t) =2t^3.$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
By the chain rule, we have 

$$
(\mathbf f \circ u)'(t) = \mathbf{f}'(u(t)) u'(t).
$$

Now, let's find the derivative of each function:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(u) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}u}(\operatorname{ln}⁡u)\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}u}({u}^{2}+5)\,j+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}u}(4u)k \\  & =\frac{1}{u}\,i+2u\,j+4\,k, \\ {u}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2{t}^{3})=6{t}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}(f∘u)^{′}(t) & ={f}^{′}(u(t)){u}^{′}(t) \\  & =(\frac{1}{u(t)}\,i+2u(t)\,j+4\,k){u}^{′}(t) \\  & =(\frac{1}{2{t}^{3}}\,i+2(2{t}^{3})\,j+4\,k)\cdot 6{t}^{2} \\  & =\frac{3}{t}\,i+24{t}^{5}\,j+24{t}^{2}\,k.\end{aligned}
$$

canonical_examples.knowledge_point: Using the Product Rules for Differentiation
canonical_examples.problem:
Find $\dfrac{\textrm d}{\textrm dt} (\mathbf f \cdot \mathbf g)(t),$ given the following functions $\mathbf f(t)$ and $\mathbf g(t)\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(t) & =\sqrt{t}\,i+{t}^{2}j \\ g(t) & =\frac{1}{t}i+{e}^{t}j\end{aligned}
$$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
Using the dot product rule, we have

$$
\dfrac{\textrm d}{\textrm dt}(\mathbf{f} \cdot \mathbf{g})(t) = \dfrac{\textrm d}{\textrm dt}(\mathbf{f}(t)) \cdot \mathbf{g}(t) + \mathbf{f}(t) \cdot \dfrac{\textrm d}{\textrm dt}(\mathbf{g}(t))
$$

Let's now find the derivatives of each function:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}f(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\sqrt{t})i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2})j \\  & =\frac{1}{2\sqrt{t}}\,i+2t\,j, \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}g(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{1}{t})i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{t})j \\  & =-\frac{1}{{t}^{2}}\,i+{e}^{t}\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\eqalign{
\dfrac{\textrm d}{\textrm dt} (\mathbf f \cdot \mathbf g)(t)
&= \dfrac{\textrm d}{\textrm dt}(\mathbf{f}(t)) \cdot \mathbf{g}(t) + \mathbf{f}(t) \cdot \dfrac{\textrm d}{\textrm dt}(\mathbf{g}(t)) \[3pt]
&= \left(\dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{t}} \,\mathbf i +2t \, \mathbf j \right) \cdot \left(\dfrac{1}{t} \,  \mathbf i + e^t \,  \mathbf j \right) +
\left(\sqrt{t} \,  \mathbf i + t^2 \,  \mathbf j \right) \cdot \left(-\dfrac{1}{t^2}  \, \mathbf i + e^t \, \mathbf j  \right) \[3pt]		 
&=\dfrac{1}{2t\sqrt{t}}  +2te^t    +  \left(-\dfrac{\sqrt{t}}{t^2}\right)    + t^2e^t \[3pt]
&=\dfrac{\sqrt{t}}{2t^2}  -  \dfrac{\sqrt{t}}{t^2} +2te^t   + t^2e^t  \[3pt]
&= -\dfrac{\sqrt{t}}{2t^2} +\left(2t+t^2\right)e^t.
}
$$
